instruction: Modify the slide layout so it uses A4 paper dimensions: 210mm x 297mm.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: This task requires changing the slide size to A4 paper format (210mm x 297mm, which equals 8.27" x 11.69"). The original file is 10.88" x 8.13". The evaluator checks if the slide dimensions match A4 paper size within 0.1 inch tolerance using a custom metric function.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts slide dimensions using python-pptx library (presentation.slide_width and presentation.slide_height)
Proper unit conversion from EMUs to inches (914400 EMUs = 1 inch) is implemented
Comparison logic correctly checks both width and height against A4 expected values (8.27" x 11.69") within 0.1 inch tolerance
Postconfig appropriately saves the file (Ctrl+S) before verification, ensuring the getter retrieves updated state
Expected values are semantically correct: A4 paper is indeed 210mm x 297mm = 8.27" x 11.69"
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' by directly accessing expected.get('width_inches') and expected.get('height_inches')
Complete coverage: verifies all requirements in the instruction (both width and height dimensions for A4 format)
Data flow is correct: file saved → vm_file getter retrieves .pptx → metric reads dimensions → compares to expected
